en.name: Rose of Viterbo
en.summary: Italian teenage visionary and street preacher who publicly opposed a hostile emperor and endured exile before dying at only seventeen.
en.body: Rose of Viterbo reported visions of the Virgin Mary as a young child and began preaching in the streets of her Italian hometown as a young teenager, urging the townspeople to remain loyal to the Pope against the political and military pressure of Emperor Frederick II, who was then in open conflict with the papacy and had significant support within Viterbo itself. Her outspoken public preaching against the emperor's faction, remarkable for a girl still only in her early teens, made her enough of a political liability that the town's pro-imperial authorities banished her and her family from Viterbo; she and her family lived in exile until Frederick's death allowed their return. She sought entry to a local convent of Poor Clares but was turned away, reportedly on account of having no dowry, and continued living as a laywoman devoted to prayer and preaching until her death in 1251 at only seventeen. Her veneration has been continuously observed in Viterbo for centuries, though she was never formally canonized through the Church's full process, and she is venerated locally with papal approval rather than under a formal canonization decree.
